nodes.name: Matching brackets with a stack
nodes.description: Push each opener; on a closer the top must be its matching opener. Balanced means every closer matched and the stack ends empty.

facets.recognize: Uses a stack whenever nesting must be checked across several bracket types.
facets.implement: Compares types, handles a closer on an empty stack and checks for leftovers.
facets.trace: Can show the stack after each character.

misconceptions.desc: Matched any closer with any opener without comparing their types.
Used one counter for several bracket types, so "([)]" passed.

nodes.name: Stack that tracks a running minimum
nodes.description: Push the running minimum with each value (or an encoded value) so the minimum is available in O(1) after any pop.

facets.explain: Explains why one min variable is not enough once the minimum is popped.
facets.implement: Stores (value, min so far) pairs, or a second stack of minimums.
facets.adapt: Uses the O(1)-space encoding 2 * value - min in long long.

misconceptions.desc: Kept one min variable, which is wrong after the minimum is popped.
In the O(1)-space encoding, computed 2 * value - min in int and overflowed.
Scanned the stack for the minimum on every getMin (O(n)).

nodes.name: Converting infix, prefix and postfix
nodes.description: Infix to postfix keeps an operator stack ordered by precedence and associativity; prefix and postfix conversions keep a stack of operand strings.

facets.explain: Explains precedence, associativity and why postfix needs no parentheses.
facets.implement: Pops by precedence, handles parentheses, and combines operands in the right order for the scan direction.
facets.trace: Can show the stack and output after each token.

misconceptions.desc: Popped operators of lower precedence, or did not pop equal precedence for left-associative operators.
Treated ^ as left-associative.
Did not pop until '(' on ')', or let '(' reach the output.
Combined two operands in the wrong order for the scan direction (prefix scans right to left).

nodes.name: Monotonic stack
nodes.description: Keep a stack whose values stay increasing or decreasing; popping the elements a new one beats answers 'next greater / smaller' for all of them in O(n) total.

facets.recognize: Spots next/previous greater or smaller element questions, spans and nearest boundaries.
facets.explain: Explains why each element is pushed and popped once, so the inner loop is O(n) overall.
facets.implement: Chooses the stack order, scan direction and comparison that answer the question.
facets.trace: Can show the stack after each element.
facets.adapt: Handles circular arrays (2n passes with i % n), previous versus next, and equal values.

misconceptions.desc: Kept the stack in the wrong order, so it answered a different question (next smaller instead of next greater).
Stored values where indices were needed for widths or distances.
For a circular array, did not loop 2n times with i % n.
Used < where <= was needed when popping (or the reverse), mishandling equal values.
Used nested loops (O(n²)) for next greater or smaller elements.
Cannot explain why a while loop inside the for loop is still O(n) overall.

nodes.name: Counting each element's contribution
nodes.description: Count the subarrays in which an element is the minimum (or maximum) from its previous and next smaller distances, and add value times that count.

facets.explain: Explains why left distance times right distance counts the subarrays where an element is the minimum.
facets.implement: Breaks ties on one side only and accumulates in long long, with the modulus if required.

misconceptions.desc: Used strict comparisons on both sides, so subarrays with equal minimums were counted twice or not at all.
Accumulated without long long or without the required modulus.
Enumerated every subarray (O(n²)) instead of counting contributions.

nodes.name: Simulating cancellation with a stack
nodes.description: Push items and let each new one cancel or merge with the top for as long as the rule applies (asteroid collisions, removing digits).

facets.implement: Keeps resolving against the top in a loop, handles ties and cleans up the result.
facets.trace: Can show the stack after each item.

misconceptions.desc: Resolved only one collision per new item instead of continuing while the rule applies.
Mishandled equal sizes, where both items must disappear.
After removing digits, left leading zeros or returned an empty string instead of "0".
Did not remove the leftover k digits from the end when nothing was popped.

nodes.name: Monotonic deque
nodes.description: Keep window indices in a deque with decreasing values: drop expired indices from the front and smaller values from the back; the front is the window maximum.

facets.recognize: Uses a deque for the maximum or minimum of every window of size k.
facets.implement: Stores indices, expires them from the front and pops smaller values from the back.
facets.trace: Can show the deque after each index.

misconceptions.desc: Did not remove indices that fell out of the window from the front.
Stored values instead of indices, so expiry could not be checked.
Rescanned each window or used a heap without expiry (O(n k)) instead of a deque.

nodes.name: Largest rectangle in a histogram
nodes.description: For each bar, width = next smaller index - previous smaller index - 1; one monotonic-stack pass finds both. A binary matrix becomes one histogram per row.

facets.explain: Explains why each bar's best rectangle spans to its nearest smaller bars.
facets.implement: Computes widths correctly when the stack empties and flushes the remaining bars at the end.
facets.adapt: Builds per-row heights for maximal rectangles in a binary matrix.

misconceptions.desc: Computed the width wrongly when the stack became empty (the width runs to the start).
Did not process bars left on the stack at the end (append a zero-height bar).
For a binary matrix, did not reset a column's height to 0 on a 0 cell.

nodes.name: Trapping rain water
nodes.description: Water over a bar = min(highest bar on its left, highest on its right) - its height; use prefix and suffix maxima, or two pointers moving the lower side.

facets.explain: Explains why the lower of the two maxima limits the water, and why the lower side can move.
facets.implement: Writes the prefix/suffix version or the two-pointer version without negative water.

misconceptions.desc: With two pointers, moved the taller side instead of the shorter one.
Left the bar itself out of its left and right maxima, giving negative water.
Recomputed the left and right maxima for every index (O(n²)).

nodes.name: Cache design (LRU, LFU)
nodes.description: A hashmap finds a key's node in O(1); a doubly linked list keeps recency order so the least recently used node is removed in O(1). LFU keeps one such list per frequency.

facets.explain: Explains why both structures are needed for O(1) get and put.
facets.implement: Moves an entry to the front on get and put, and removes the evicted node from both structures.
facets.adapt: Extends to LFU with per-frequency lists and a tracked minimum frequency.

misconceptions.desc: Did not move an entry to the front on get, only on put.
On put of an existing key, added a second node instead of updating and moving the first.
Removed the evicted node from the list but not its key from the map, or the reverse.
Tracked recency with timestamps and scanned for the oldest entry (O(n) eviction).
In LFU, did not update the minimum frequency when its list emptied, or broke ties without recency.

nodes.name: Eliminating candidates in pairs
nodes.description: Compare two candidates; one comparison rules one of them out, so n - 1 comparisons leave a single candidate to verify.

facets.explain: Explains why one comparison always rules out one candidate.
facets.implement: Eliminates with two pointers or a stack, then verifies the survivor.

misconceptions.desc: Returned the remaining candidate without verifying it.
Checked every row and column (O(n²)) instead of eliminating.
